book.title: Anger: Wisdom for Cooling the Flames
book.author: Thich Nhat Hanh

confidence_note: Baby quote is verbatim; mother-strikes-baby passage and 'mothers of our own anger' from a summary of the text.
facts: Anger is like a howling baby, suffering and crying; the baby needs his mother to embrace him.
One passage pictures a mother striking her crying baby, failing to see she and the child are one.
We are the mothers of our own anger.
A good mother picks the baby up, speaks quietly, looks for what makes it cry.
Mindful breathing gives the caring energy of a mother; embracing anger and breathing is enough.
Try not to say or do anything when angry.
tension: We shout at our own anger instead of holding it.
opening_idea: A howling baby with no one turning round.

lessons.idea: Hold your anger instead of scolding it.

reflect_final: Next time anger arrives like a crying baby, what is the first small thing you do to take it in your arms?

use_cases.situation: Scolding yourself after a tense meeting
use_cases.move: My anger is like a crying baby, so I won't shout at it.
Give me a minute, I'm angry too. I'll breathe and then listen.

use_cases.situation: A friend tells you how angry they are
use_cases.move: You don't have to push it down. I'm here, tell me.

pocket_idea: If anger is a crying baby, do not shout at it. Hold it with your breath.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Anger is a howling baby that needs holding.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Baby image, mother who strikes baby, breathing, not speaking.
